newsitem.title: USA: Meat processor recalls burger because of E.coli.
newsitem.headline: Meat processor recalls burger because of E.coli.

text.p: U.S. meat processor Hudson Foods Co. is recalling 20,000 pounds of frozen ground beef patties nationwide because the meat may be contaminated with the potentially deadly E.coli O157:H7 bacteria, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday.
It said it learned about the problem from Colorado health officials after several consumers in the state who had eaten hamburger in early July became ill.

The meat was distributed nationwide in June and early July and is not likely to be still on shop shelves, the department said. But since the meat was sold frozen, consumers may still have some stored in their freezers, it said.

"USDA is informing the public so consumers who may have purchased and stored (the) product in their freezers around that time can know to check," said Thomas Billy, head of the department's Food Safety and Inspection Service.

Hudson Foods, of Rogers, Arkansas, is voluntarily recalling 48-ounce packages of "Hudson Beef Burgers, Individually Quick Frozen" with the code "156A7"; three-pound packages of "Hudson 100% Pure Beef Patties, Individually Frozen" with the code "156B7" and 15-pound boxes of "Hudson 60 - 1/4 Beef Patties Uncooked, Individually Quick Frozen" with the code "155B7."

The potentially lethal E.coli O157:H7 can cause bloody diarrhoea and dehydration. Four years ago, 500 people became ill and four children died as in the Pacific Northwest as a result of eating fast-food restaurant hamburgers tainted with the bacteria.
